(1) massive early-type galaxies lie on the mass-plane with small intrinsic scatter and (2) the structure parameter ce2 of these galaxies is not strongly sensitive to the details of the mass distribution and anisotropies.

the question: what is special about the mass–radius–velocity dispersion scaling relations of massive, early-type galaxies?
the question of whether the mass plane of early-type galaxies can be understood as a consequence of the mass–density profile and orbital anisotropic structure of these objects.

the mass plane is not very sensitive to the mass and velocity anisotropy distribution, but it is sensitive to the mass density profile.
the observed scatter in ce2 is consistent with most plausible families of spherical models for massive early-type galaxies.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the MP is an extremely robust relation that constrains the internal structure and orbital properties of early-type galaxies.
a wide range of galaxy models can reproduce the observed MP, and the MP is therefore a relatively weak discriminant between models.
